note: The checker's own quick-mode answers on fixed setups, in its own words. answerKind says what kind of answer each is (a RigCheck capacity estimate, a planning budget, a published route or recipe match); none is a measured setup. tier 'na' means unknown, not 'does not fit'. Conditions are part of the answer.

tiers.good: an answer without caveats of the checker's own kind; a limit stated in the answer (such as raising a Mac's GPU wired-memory limit, macLimit) still applies
tiers.caveats: an answer with caveats (part in system RAM, a planning estimate, an unverified peak or route)
tiers.no: does not fit, or below the smallest published figure
tiers.na: unknown: the checker covers no route or source for this hardware

answers.answer: Matches DwarfStar's 128 GB route: Q2 with SSD streaming (September weights)
answers.conditions: DwarfStar runs its Q2 file (365.7 GB) on one 128 GB Mac by streaming routed experts from SSD (--ssd-streaming), with the expert cache sized automatically. DwarfStar publishes no V4.1 speed for a 128 GB Mac (its one Mac figure is Q4 resident on a 512 GB M3 Ultra). Two 128 GB machines can instead hold it resident with tensor parallelism (set machines to two). DwarfStar's guide now documents its Q2 setups with the 1017 file; this September file is still in its repository, and its V4.1 speeds were measured with it. Image input works on Metal with its separate 0.97 GB vision encoder. DwarfStar is a community engine, not DeepSeek's code; these are its documented setups, not a RigCheck estimate. Keep the GGUF on a fast local SSD (the 189 GiB of Engram tables are always read from the file).

answers.answer: Matches DwarfStar's 128 GB route: Q2 with SSD streaming (1017 weights)
answers.conditions: DwarfStar runs its Q2 file (365.7 GB) on one 128 GB Mac by streaming routed experts from SSD (--ssd-streaming), with the expert cache sized automatically. Two 128 GB machines can instead hold it resident with tensor parallelism (set machines to two). DwarfStar's V4.1 guide documents these setups with its 1017 Q2 file, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-IQ2_XXS-Q2_K-imatrix.gguf (read October 24, 2026); its V4.1 speeds were all measured with its September file, before the 1017 file existed, so none is given here. Image input works on Metal with its separate 0.97 GB vision encoder (DwarfStar's guide pairs it with the 1017 file). DwarfStar is a community engine, not DeepSeek's code; these are its documented setups, not a RigCheck estimate. Keep the GGUF on a fast local SSD (the 189 GiB of Engram tables are always read from the file). Experimental alternative for 1017: Unsloth says its UD-IQ1_S GGUF (233.0 GB, its 110.6 GB Engram table on SSD via mmap) works on 128 GB RAM setups such as a MacBook, DGX Spark or RTX Spark; its 128–145 GB RAM plus VRAM estimate for 1-bit is the top of a 128 GB machine (runtime and context can need more). It runs in Unsloth's unmerged llama.cpp pull request #30817 branch or Unsloth Desktop, no published speed.

answers.answer: Matches DwarfStar: Q2 or Q4 fully resident on a 512 GB Mac (September weights)
answers.conditions: DwarfStar names a 512 GB Mac as the resident target for its Q4 file (518.6 GB in two parts; 294.15 GiB of main weights) and says full residency was tested on an M3 Ultra with 512 GB. Its Q2 file (152 GiB of main weights) also fits resident on any 256 GB or larger Mac. DwarfStar's QA record for Q4 fully resident on a 512 GB M3 Ultra (36,864-token allocation, medians of three sweeps): 341.75 tokens/s prefill and 18.69 tokens/s generation at a 4,096-token context, 18.11 tokens/s generation at 32,768. That is the only published Mac speed for V4.1: M3 Ultra with Q4, none for Q2 or the M5 Ultra. Image input works on Metal with its separate 0.97 GB vision encoder. DwarfStar is a community engine, not DeepSeek's code; these are its documented setups, not a RigCheck estimate. Keep the GGUF on a fast local SSD (the 189 GiB of Engram tables are always read from the file).
